$$
T(s)=\frac{1}{2}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{s},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{s},\,\sqrt{3}⟩.
$$" :question/worked-solution "Since we are given that the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature: 

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖
$$

Now, we differentiate $T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and evaluate it at $s={\pi }^{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{s}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{s}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\sqrt{3})⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{s}}{2\sqrt{s}},\,\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{s}}{2\sqrt{s}},\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4\sqrt{s}}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{s},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{s},\,0⟩ \\ {T}^{′}({\pi }^{2}) & =\frac{1}{4\sqrt{{\pi }^{2}}}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{{\pi }^{2}},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{{\pi }^{2}},\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4\pi }⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4\pi }⟨0,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we obtain the curvature:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ({\pi }^{2}) & =‖{T}^{′}({\pi }^{2})‖ \\  & =\frac{1}{4\pi }\cdot \sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{4\pi }\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-c322fadd-ac27-57ed-bf43-9e8ac0bbc8e8"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "q-131732" :question/problem "Consider the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by arc length $s.$ Find the curvature at the point where $s=0$ if the unit tangent vector of the curve is given by

$$
T(s)=\frac{1}{5}⟨-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{10}),\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{10}),\,3⟩.
$$" :question/worked-solution "Since we are given that the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature: 

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖
$$

Now, we differentiate $T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and evaluate it at $s=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =\frac{1}{5}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{10})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{10})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(3)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨-\frac{2}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{10}),\,-\frac{2}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{10}),\,0⟩ \\  & =-\frac{2}{25}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{10}),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{10}),\,0⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(0) & =-\frac{2}{25}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(0),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(0),\,0⟩ \\  & =-\frac{2}{25}⟨1,0,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we obtain the curvature:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(0) & =‖{T}^{′}(0)‖ \\  & =\frac{2}{25}\cdot \sqrt{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{25}\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-d272c7ef-b48e-5924-96ef-203f6d488dc4"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id {:db/id "question-c4f686a5-889f-5e90-8c7e-36ce4fec4b92" :question/id #uuid "c4f686a5-889f-5e90-8c7e-36ce4fec4b92" :question/math-academy-id "q-80521" :question/problem "Consider the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by arc length $s.$ Find the curvature at the point where $s=2{\pi }^{2}$ if the unit tangent vector of the curve is given by

 

$$
T(s)=\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{2s}\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{2s}\,j.
$$" :question/worked-solution "Since we are given that the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖
$$

Now, we differentiate $T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and evaluate it at $s=2{\pi }^{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{2s})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{2s})\,j \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{2s}}{\sqrt{2s}}\,i+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{2s}}{\sqrt{2s}}\,j \\ {T}^{′}(2{\pi }^{2}) & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{2(2{\pi }^{2})}}{\sqrt{2(2{\pi }^{2})}}\,i+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{2(2{\pi }^{2})}}{\sqrt{2(2{\pi }^{2})}}\,j \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )}{2\pi }\,i+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )}{2\pi }\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }\,j\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we obtain the curvature:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(2{\pi }^{2}) & =‖{T}^{′}(2{\pi }^{2})‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{(0)}^{2}+{(\frac{1}{2\pi })}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-70818e4d-0bd1-5756-b56e-538edbd5bffe"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-70818e4d-0bd1-5756-b56e-538edbd5bffe" :answer-field/id #uuid "70818e4d-0bd1-5756-b56e-538edbd5bffe" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-9372156d-f747-53e5-bf4d-3dde0aba7079" :answer-field/choices ["answer-c9a83a8d-c1c5-5b09-a81e-6dcef9136233" "answer-9372156d-f747-53e5-bf4d-3dde0aba7079" "answer-2be96d5c-0914-5fe5-acba-da0c7e6d8b3a" "answer-5616aca8-3b97-5fdd-9cff-fae082d196cd" "answer-5562ffbc-ebce-5ef5-a7e7-e05b1cb533d7"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-c9a83a8d-c1c5-5b09-a81e-6dcef9136233" :answer/id #uuid "c9a83a8d-c1c5-5b09-a81e-6dcef9136233" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2\pi " :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-9372156d-f747-53e5-bf4d-3dde0aba7079" :answer/id #uuid "9372156d-f747-53e5-bf4d-3dde0aba7079" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{2\pi }" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-2be96d5c-0914-5fe5-acba-da0c7e6d8b3a" :answer/id #uuid "2be96d5c-0914-5fe5-acba-da0c7e6d8b3a" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{\pi }" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-5616aca8-3b97-5fdd-9cff-fae082d196cd" :answer/id #uuid "5616aca8-3b97-5fdd-9cff-fae082d196cd" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{2\pi }}{2\pi }" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-5562ffbc-ebce-5ef5-a7e7-e05b1cb533d7" :answer/id #uuid "5562ffbc-ebce-5ef5-a7e7-e05b1cb533d7" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\sqrt{2\pi }" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120494 :question/problem "Consider the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by arc length $s.$ Find the curvature at the point where $s=\frac{3\pi }{2}$ if the unit tangent vector of the curve is given by

$$
T(s)=⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{s}{3},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{s}{3},\,0⟩.
$$" :question/worked-solution "Since we are given that the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are both parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖
$$

Now, we differentiate $T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and evaluate it at $s=\frac{3\pi }{2}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{s}{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{s}{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{s}{3},\,-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{s}{3},\,0⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(\frac{3\pi }{2}) & =⟨-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{3\pi }{2}),\,-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{3\pi }{2}),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-\frac{1}{3},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain the curvature:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(\frac{3\pi }{2}) & =‖{T}^{′}(\frac{3\pi }{2})‖=\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{2}+{0}^{2}}=\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186119078 :answer-field/correct 17592186119080 :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "question-84ec701f-8d6f-546b-8f54-4258332a1413" :question/id #uuid "84ec701f-8d6f-546b-8f54-4258332a1413" :question/math-academy-id "q-131743" :question/problem "Consider the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by arc length $s.$ Find the curvature at the point where $s=\frac{\pi }{4}$ if the unit tangent vector of the curve is given by

$$
T(s)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡s,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡s,\,\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s⟩.
$$" :question/worked-solution "Since we are given that the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature: 

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖
$$

Now, we differentiate $T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and evaluate it at $s=\frac{\pi }{4}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡s,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡s,\,-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}),\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}),\,-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},-1⟩ \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}⟨1,1,\sqrt{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we obtain the curvature:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖ \\  & =‖-\frac{1}{2}⟨1,1,\sqrt{2}⟩‖ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(\sqrt{2})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2 \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-e894091a-2e63-5373-8285-532c7e949b88"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-e894091a-2e63-5373-8285-532c7e949b88" :answer-field/id #uuid "e894091a-2e63-5373-8285-532c7e949b88" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-206b9917-9249-5d96-885f-9052cced1472" :answer-field/choices ["answer-206b9917-9249-5d96-885f-9052cced1472" "answer-82909bce-1b68-5d11-be22-86b127324a90" "answer-e34cad78-7ce1-5b5b-aa1e-1145d9440cd7" "answer-bdc52b86-edc3-5ab3-8c53-46f3784df89f" "answer-38a62d49-ab80-5de1-b7d6-df3c195fadb0"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-206b9917-9249-5d96-885f-9052cced1472" :answer/id #uuid "206b9917-9249-5d96-885f-9052cced1472" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "1" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-82909bce-1b68-5d11-be22-86b127324a90" :answer/id #uuid "82909bce-1b68-5d11-be22-86b127324a90" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-e34cad78-7ce1-5b5b-aa1e-1145d9440cd7" :answer/id #uuid "e34cad78-7ce1-5b5b-aa1e-1145d9440cd7" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-bdc52b86-edc3-5ab3-8c53-46f3784df89f" :answer/id #uuid "bdc52b86-edc3-5ab3-8c53-46f3784df89f" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-38a62d49-ab80-5de1-b7d6-df3c195fadb0" :answer/id #uuid "38a62d49-ab80-5de1-b7d6-df3c195fadb0" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{4}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-d96a6265-af2d-5821-9fbc-e9e0d0216e3e" :question/id #uuid "d96a6265-af2d-5821-9fbc-e9e0d0216e3e" :question/math-academy-id "q-131945" :question/problem "Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where

$$
r(s)=⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\frac{4}{5}s⟩,\,0\le s<10\pi .
$$" :question/worked-solution "Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{4}{5}s)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,\frac{4}{5}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,4⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =\frac{1}{5}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(4)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,0⟩ \\  & =-\frac{3}{25}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =|-\frac{3}{25}|\cdot \sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{5})+{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{5})+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3}{25}\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{3}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-92b6ebf7-c2b9-5972-b09e-a6f7847a9371"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-92b6ebf7-c2b9-5972-b09e-a6f7847a9371" :answer-field/id #uuid "92b6ebf7-c2b9-5972-b09e-a6f7847a9371" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-5af6f583-3aa5-5c21-9b27-812d24aaba4e" :answer-field/choices ["answer-f6f59c1d-0707-55ca-b46e-a15a0d3ed556" "answer-5af6f583-3aa5-5c21-9b27-812d24aaba4e" "answer-a2a2861c-388d-58fc-af3f-6ca10eb128d3" "answer-eda35170-2016-5f0d-84da-1b5c4583cefb" "answer-625782b0-4ad1-5de1-8987-e95b17c343ec"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-f6f59c1d-0707-55ca-b46e-a15a0d3ed556" :answer/id #uuid "f6f59c1d-0707-55ca-b46e-a15a0d3ed556" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{5}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-5af6f583-3aa5-5c21-9b27-812d24aaba4e" :answer/id #uuid "5af6f583-3aa5-5c21-9b27-812d24aaba4e" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{3}{25}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a2a2861c-388d-58fc-af3f-6ca10eb128d3" :answer/id #uuid "a2a2861c-388d-58fc-af3f-6ca10eb128d3" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{3}{5}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-eda35170-2016-5f0d-84da-1b5c4583cefb" :answer/id #uuid "eda35170-2016-5f0d-84da-1b5c4583cefb" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{9}{25}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-625782b0-4ad1-5de1-8987-e95b17c343ec" :answer/id #uuid "625782b0-4ad1-5de1-8987-e95b17c343ec" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{9}{5}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120326 :question/problem "Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where

$$

$$" :question/worked-solution "Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$

$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}))⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}},\,-3\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}),\,3\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}})⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}⟨1,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}),\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}})⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(1),\,-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}),\,3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}})⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}⟨0,\,-3\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}),\,-3\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}})⟩ \\  & =\frac{3}{10}⟨0,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}),\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}})⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$

$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186118095 :answer-field/correct 17592186118099 :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "question-a4a4a281-bd0c-502e-a09a-cc4e77ac53a7" :question/id #uuid "a4a4a281-bd0c-502e-a09a-cc4e77ac53a7" :question/math-academy-id "q-83643" :question/problem "Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where:

$$" :question/worked-solution "Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

"question-941975f4-ea50-5edb-a299-e8568f71e188" :question/id #uuid "941975f4-ea50-5edb-a299-e8568f71e188" :question/math-academy-id "q-83663" :question/problem "Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)$ given that its derivative ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the corresponding unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$ are as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)=\,-12{t}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{3})i+12{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{3})\,j,\,{T}^{′}(t)=-3{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{3})\,i-3{t}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{3})\,j\end{aligned}
$$" :question/worked-solution "Since we are given both the derivative of the curve ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we find the magnitudes of ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-12{t}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{3}))}^{2}+{(12{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{3}))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-12{t}^{2})^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡({t}^{3})+(12{t}^{2})^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡({t}^{3})} \\  & =\sqrt{(12{t}^{2})^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡({t}^{3})+{cos}^{2}⁡({t}^{3}))} \\  & =12{t}^{2} \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-3{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{3}))}^{2}+{(-3{t}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{3}))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-3{t}^{2})^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡({t}^{3})+(-3{t}^{2})^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡({t}^{3})} \\  & =\sqrt{(3{t}^{2})^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡({t}^{3})+{cos}^{2}⁡({t}^{3}))} \\  & =3{t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{3{t}^{2}}{12{t}^{2}}=\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-d2ae9bf6-e514-5558-98b8-e081859740e5"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-d2ae9bf6-e514-5558-98b8-e081859740e5" :answer-field/id #uuid "d2ae9bf6-e514-5558-98b8-e081859740e5" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-3c9b736d-97b9-5346-ae4c-3f48e12a4b99" :answer-field/choices ["answer-ac11b4df-2cb6-5f6b-92fb-3e07ba50cb5b" "answer-c2b8e622-9766-5512-823c-41c899359c51" "answer-4efce17f-3075-5e92-ad94-a11200baf0b2" "answer-8d0a7ca2-651b-528e-afe7-bc816f290417" "answer-3c9b736d-97b9-5346-ae4c-3f48e12a4b99"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-ac11b4df-2cb6-5f6b-92fb-3e07ba50cb5b" :answer/id #uuid "ac11b4df-2cb6-5f6b-92fb-3e07ba50cb5b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "0" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-c2b8e622-9766-5512-823c-41c899359c51" :answer/id #uuid "c2b8e622-9766-5512-823c-41c899359c51" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-4efce17f-3075-5e92-ad94-a11200baf0b2" :answer/id #uuid "4efce17f-3075-5e92-ad94-a11200baf0b2" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8d0a7ca2-651b-528e-afe7-bc816f290417" :answer/id #uuid "8d0a7ca2-651b-528e-afe7-bc816f290417" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3c9b736d-97b9-5346-ae4c-3f48e12a4b99" :answer/id #uuid "3c9b736d-97b9-5346-ae4c-3f48e12a4b99" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{4}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186121002 :tutorial/content "The **curvature** of a curve measures how much the curve "bends" at a given point. It can also be thought of as a measure of how much the curve deviates from being a straight line. Curvature is denoted by the Greek letter $\kappa$ (pronounced "kappa"). 

If $\kappa=0$ at some point on a curve, then that curve looks like a straight line in some neighborhood of the point.

If the curve $\mathbf{r}(s)$ is parametrized by the arc length $s,$ then the curvature $\kappa$ is the magnitude of the change of direction of the unit tangent vector $\mathbf T$ per unit of arc length. That is,

$$
\kappa(s) = \left\| \dfrac{\textrm{d}\mathbf T}{\textrm{d}s}  \right\|= \| \mathbf T'(s) \|.
$$

Note that $|| \mathbf v ||$ denotes the magnitude of the vector $\mathbf v.$

For example, suppose we are given the curve 

$$
\mathbf r(s)= \left\langle \sin\left(\dfrac s2\right), \: \dfrac{\sqrt{3}s}{2}, \: -\cos\left(\dfrac s2\right)\right\rangle
$$

 
which is parametrized by arc length $s.$ Let's find the curvature of  $\mathbf r(s)$  at the point where $s={\pi}.$

First, we find the unit tangent vector:

$$
\mathbf T(s) =\dfrac 12 \left\langle \cos\left( \dfrac s2\right), \: \sqrt{3}, \: \sin \left(\dfrac s2\right)\right\rangle
$$

 

Next, we differentiate $\mathbf{T}(s)$ and evaluate its absolute value at $s=\pi\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\sqrt{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2}))⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,0,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(\pi ) & =\frac{1}{4}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,0,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}⟨-1,\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain the curvature by taking the magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(\pi ) & =‖{T}^{′}(\pi )‖=\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{0}^{2}}=\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

 

**Note:** To calculate $\kappa,$ the function $\mathbf{r}(s)$ should be at least twice differentiable with respect to $s.$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186121007 :tutorial/content "If the curve $\mathbf r(t)$ is parametrized by a general parameter $t,$ then

$$
\kappa(t) = \dfrac{\|\mathbf T'(t)\|}{\|\mathbf r'(t)\|}.
$$

To understand why this is, remember that the arc length $s$ and the parameter $t$ are related by the formula 

$$
\displaystyle s(t)= \int_0^t\left\| \mathbf  r'(x)\right\|\, \textrm dx.
$$

By the chain rule and the fundamental theorem of calculus, then, we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d  \mathbf T}{\textrm d t} = \dfrac{\textrm d  \mathbf T}{\textrm d s} \dfrac{\textrm d  s}{\textrm d t}= \dfrac{\textrm d  \mathbf T}{\textrm d s} \left\| \mathbf r'(t)\right\|.
$$

  

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖\frac{\text{d}T}{\text{d}t}‖ & =‖\frac{\text{d}T}{\text{d}s}‖‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =κ(t)‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ \\ κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120033 :activity/expected-seconds 1020.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]}]

$$
T(s)=\frac{1}{2}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{s},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{s},\,\sqrt{3}⟩.
$$" :question/worked-solution "Since we are given that the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

parametrized by arc length $s.$ Find the curvature at the point where $s=2{\pi }^{2}$ if the unit tangent vector of the curve is given by

 

$$
T(s)=\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{2s}\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{2s}\,j.
$$" :question/worked-solution "Since we are given that the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{2s})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{2s})\,j \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{2s}}{\sqrt{2s}}\,i+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{2s}}{\sqrt{2s}}\,j \\ {T}^{′}(2{\pi }^{2}) & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{2(2{\pi }^{2})}}{\sqrt{2(2{\pi }^{2})}}\,i+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{2(2{\pi }^{2})}}{\sqrt{2(2{\pi }^{2})}}\,j \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )}{2\pi }\,i+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )}{2\pi }\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }\,j\end{aligned}

$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-70818e4d-0bd1-5756-b56e-538edbd5bffe"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-70818e4d-0bd1-5756-b56e-538edbd5bffe" :answer-field/id #uuid "70818e4d-0bd1-5756-b56e-538edbd5bffe" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-9372156d-f747-53e5-bf4d-3dde0aba7079" :answer-field/choices ["answer-c9a83a8d-c1c5-5b09-a81e-6dcef9136233" "answer-9372156d-f747-53e5-bf4d-3dde0aba7079" "answer-2be96d5c-0914-5fe5-acba-da0c7e6d8b3a" "answer-5616aca8-3b97-5fdd-9cff-fae082d196cd" "answer-5562ffbc-ebce-5ef5-a7e7-e05b1cb533d7"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-c9a83a8d-c1c5-5b09-a81e-6dcef9136233" :answer/id #uuid "c9a83a8d-c1c5-5b09-a81e-6dcef9136233" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2\pi " :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-9372156d-f747-53e5-bf4d-3dde0aba7079" :answer/id #uuid "9372156d-f747-53e5-bf4d-3dde0aba7079" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{2\pi }" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-2be96d5c-0914-5fe5-acba-da0c7e6d8b3a" :answer/id #uuid "2be96d5c-0914-5fe5-acba-da0c7e6d8b3a" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{\pi }" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-5616aca8-3b97-5fdd-9cff-fae082d196cd" :answer/id #uuid "5616aca8-3b97-5fdd-9cff-fae082d196cd" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{2\pi }}{2\pi }" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-5562ffbc-ebce-5ef5-a7e7-e05b1cb533d7" :answer/id #uuid "5562ffbc-ebce-5ef5-a7e7-e05b1cb533d7" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\sqrt{2\pi }" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120494 :question/problem "Consider the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by arc length $s.$ Find the curvature at the point where $s=\frac{3\pi }{2}$ if the unit tangent vector of the curve is given by

$$
T(s)=⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{s}{3},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{s}{3},\,0⟩.
$$" :question/worked-solution "Since we are given that the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are both parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖
$$

Now, we differentiate $T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and evaluate it at $s=\frac{3\pi }{2}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{s}{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{s}{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{s}{3},\,-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{s}{3},\,0⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(\frac{3\pi }{2}) & =⟨-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{3\pi }{2}),\,-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{3\pi }{2}),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-\frac{1}{3},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain the curvature:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(\frac{3\pi }{2}) & =‖{T}^{′}(\frac{3\pi }{2})‖=\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{2}+{0}^{2}}=\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186119078 :answer-field/correct 17592186119080 :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "question-84ec701f-8d6f-546b-8f54-4258332a1413" :question/id #uuid "84ec701f-8d6f-546b-8f54-4258332a1413" :question/math-academy-id "q-131743" :question/problem "Consider the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by arc length $s.$ Find the curvature at the point where $s=\frac{\pi }{4}$ if the unit tangent vector of the curve is given by

$$
T(s)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡s,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡s,\,\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s⟩.
$$" :question/worked-solution "Since we are given that the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature: 

$$

Finally, we obtain the curvature:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖ \\  & =‖-\frac{1}{2}⟨1,1,\sqrt{2}⟩‖ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(\sqrt{2})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2 \\  & =1\end{aligned}

$$
r(s)=⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\frac{4}{5}s⟩,\,0\le s<10\pi .
$$" :question/worked-solution "Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{4}{5}s)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,\frac{4}{5}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,4⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =\frac{1}{5}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(4)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,0⟩ \\  & =-\frac{3}{25}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =|-\frac{3}{25}|\cdot \sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{5})+{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{5})+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3}{25}\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{3}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-92b6ebf7-c2b9-5972-b09e-a6f7847a9371"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-92b6ebf7-c2b9-5972-b09e-a6f7847a9371" :answer-field/id #uuid "92b6ebf7-c2b9-5972-b09e-a6f7847a9371" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-5af6f583-3aa5-5c21-9b27-812d24aaba4e" :answer-field/choices ["answer-f6f59c1d-0707-55ca-b46e-a15a0d3ed556" "answer-5af6f583-3aa5-5c21-9b27-812d24aaba4e" "answer-a2a2861c-388d-58fc-af3f-6ca10eb128d3" "answer-eda35170-2016-5f0d-84da-1b5c4583cefb" "answer-625782b0-4ad1-5de1-8987-e95b17c343ec"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-f6f59c1d-0707-55ca-b46e-a15a0d3ed556" :answer/id #uuid "f6f59c1d-0707-55ca-b46e-a15a0d3ed556" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{5}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-5af6f583-3aa5-5c21-9b27-812d24aaba4e" :answer/id #uuid "5af6f583-3aa5-5c21-9b27-812d24aaba4e" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{3}{25}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a2a2861c-388d-58fc-af3f-6ca10eb128d3" :answer/id #uuid "a2a2861c-388d-58fc-af3f-6ca10eb128d3" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{3}{5}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-eda35170-2016-5f0d-84da-1b5c4583cefb" :answer/id #uuid "eda35170-2016-5f0d-84da-1b5c4583cefb" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{9}{25}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-625782b0-4ad1-5de1-8987-e95b17c343ec" :answer/id #uuid "625782b0-4ad1-5de1-8987-e95b17c343ec" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{9}{5}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120326 :question/problem "Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where

$$
r(s)=⟨\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}},\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}),\,3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}})⟩,\,0\le s<2\sqrt{10}\,\pi .
$$" :question/worked-solution "Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}))⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}},\,-3\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}),\,3\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}})⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}⟨1,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}),\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}})⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(1),\,-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}),\,3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}})⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}⟨0,\,-3\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}),\,-3\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}})⟩ \\  & =\frac{3}{10}⟨0,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}),\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}})⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =\frac{3}{10}\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}))}^{2}+{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}))}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3}{10}\sqrt{0+{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}})+{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}})} \\  & =\frac{3}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186118095 :answer-field/correct 17592186118099 :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "question-a4a4a281-bd0c-502e-a09a-cc4e77ac53a7" :question/id #uuid "a4a4a281-bd0c-502e-a09a-cc4e77ac53a7" :question/math-academy-id "q-83643" :question/problem "Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where:

$$" :question/worked-solution "Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

"question-941975f4-ea50-5edb-a299-e8568f71e188" :question/id #uuid "941975f4-ea50-5edb-a299-e8568f71e188" :question/math-academy-id "q-83663" :question/problem "Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)$ given that its derivative ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the corresponding unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$ are as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)=\,-12{t}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{3})i+12{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{3})\,j,\,{T}^{′}(t)=-3{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{3})\,i-3{t}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{3})\,j\end{aligned}
$$" :question/worked-solution "Since we are given both the derivative of the curve ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we find the magnitudes of ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-12{t}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{3}))}^{2}+{(12{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{3}))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-12{t}^{2})^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡({t}^{3})+(12{t}^{2})^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡({t}^{3})} \\  & =\sqrt{(12{t}^{2})^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡({t}^{3})+{cos}^{2}⁡({t}^{3}))} \\  & =12{t}^{2} \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-3{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{3}))}^{2}+{(-3{t}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{3}))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-3{t}^{2})^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡({t}^{3})+(-3{t}^{2})^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡({t}^{3})} \\  & =\sqrt{(3{t}^{2})^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡({t}^{3})+{cos}^{2}⁡({t}^{3}))} \\  & =3{t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{3{t}^{2}}{12{t}^{2}}=\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-d2ae9bf6-e514-5558-98b8-e081859740e5"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-d2ae9bf6-e514-5558-98b8-e081859740e5" :answer-field/id #uuid "d2ae9bf6-e514-5558-98b8-e081859740e5" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-3c9b736d-97b9-5346-ae4c-3f48e12a4b99" :answer-field/choices ["answer-ac11b4df-2cb6-5f6b-92fb-3e07ba50cb5b" "answer-c2b8e622-9766-5512-823c-41c899359c51" "answer-4efce17f-3075-5e92-ad94-a11200baf0b2" "answer-8d0a7ca2-651b-528e-afe7-bc816f290417" "answer-3c9b736d-97b9-5346-ae4c-3f48e12a4b99"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-ac11b4df-2cb6-5f6b-92fb-3e07ba50cb5b" :answer/id #uuid "ac11b4df-2cb6-5f6b-92fb-3e07ba50cb5b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "0" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-c2b8e622-9766-5512-823c-41c899359c51" :answer/id #uuid "c2b8e622-9766-5512-823c-41c899359c51" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-4efce17f-3075-5e92-ad94-a11200baf0b2" :answer/id #uuid "4efce17f-3075-5e92-ad94-a11200baf0b2" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8d0a7ca2-651b-528e-afe7-bc816f290417" :answer/id #uuid "8d0a7ca2-651b-528e-afe7-bc816f290417" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3c9b736d-97b9-5346-ae4c-3f48e12a4b99" :answer/id #uuid "3c9b736d-97b9-5346-ae4c-3f48e12a4b99" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{4}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186121002 :tutorial/content "The **curvature** of a curve measures how much the curve "bends" at a given point. It can also be thought of as a measure of how much the curve deviates from being a straight line. Curvature is denoted by the Greek letter $\kappa$ (pronounced "kappa"). 

If $\kappa=0$ at some point on a curve, then that curve looks like a straight line in some neighborhood of the point.

If the curve $\mathbf{r}(s)$ is parametrized by the arc length $s,$ then the curvature $\kappa$ is the magnitude of the change of direction of the unit tangent vector $\mathbf T$ per unit of arc length. That is,

$$
\kappa(s) = \left\| \dfrac{\textrm{d}\mathbf T}{\textrm{d}s}  \right\|= \| \mathbf T'(s) \|.
$$

Note that $|| \mathbf v ||$ denotes the magnitude of the vector $\mathbf v.$

For example, suppose we are given the curve 

$$
\mathbf r(s)= \left\langle \sin\left(\dfrac s2\right), \: \dfrac{\sqrt{3}s}{2}, \: -\cos\left(\dfrac s2\right)\right\rangle
$$

 
which is parametrized by arc length $s.$ Let's find the curvature of  $\mathbf r(s)$  at the point where $s={\pi}.$

First, we find the unit tangent vector:

$$
\mathbf T(s) =\dfrac 12 \left\langle \cos\left( \dfrac s2\right), \: \sqrt{3}, \: \sin \left(\dfrac s2\right)\right\rangle
$$

 

Next, we differentiate $\mathbf{T}(s)$ and evaluate its absolute value at $s=\pi\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\sqrt{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2}))⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,0,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(\pi ) & =\frac{1}{4}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,0,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}⟨-1,\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain the curvature by taking the magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(\pi ) & =‖{T}^{′}(\pi )‖=\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{0}^{2}}=\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

 

**Note:** To calculate $\kappa,$ the function $\mathbf{r}(s)$ should be at least twice differentiable with respect to $s.$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186121007 :tutorial/content "If the curve $\mathbf r(t)$ is parametrized by a general parameter $t,$ then

$$
\kappa(t) = \dfrac{\|\mathbf T'(t)\|}{\|\mathbf r'(t)\|}.
$$

To understand why this is, remember that the arc length $s$ and the parameter $t$ are related by the formula 

$$
\displaystyle s(t)= \int_0^t\left\| \mathbf  r'(x)\right\|\, \textrm dx.
$$

By the chain rule and the fundamental theorem of calculus, then, we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d  \mathbf T}{\textrm d t} = \dfrac{\textrm d  \mathbf T}{\textrm d s} \dfrac{\textrm d  s}{\textrm d t}= \dfrac{\textrm d  \mathbf T}{\textrm d s} \left\| \mathbf r'(t)\right\|.
$$

  

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖\frac{\text{d}T}{\text{d}t}‖ & =‖\frac{\text{d}T}{\text{d}s}‖‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =κ(t)‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ \\ κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186120033 :activity/expected-seconds 1020.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]}] "assertions" [["question-4e6f234b-737b-5376-aaeb-5d730bef9b84" :question/id #uuid "4e6f234b-737b-5376-aaeb-5d730bef9b84"] ["question-4e6f234b-737b-5376-aaeb-5d730bef9b84" :question/math-academy-id "q-131742"] ["question-4e6f234b-737b-5376-aaeb-5d730bef9b84" :question/problem "Consider the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by arc length $s.$ Find the curvature at the point where $s={\pi }^{2}$ if the unit tangent vector of the curve is given by

$$
T(s)=\frac{1}{2}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{s},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{s},\,\sqrt{3}⟩.
$$"] ["question-4e6f234b-737b-5376-aaeb-5d730bef9b84" :question/worked-solution "Since we are given that the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature: 

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖
$$

Now, we differentiate $T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and evaluate it at $s={\pi }^{2}:$

$$

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{4}{5}s)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,\frac{4}{5}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,4⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =\frac{1}{5}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(4)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,0⟩ \\  & =-\frac{3}{25}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =|-\frac{3}{25}|\cdot \sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{5})+{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{5})+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3}{25}\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{3}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$"] ["question-d96a6265-af2d-5821-9fbc-e9e0d0216e3e" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] ["answer-field-92b6ebf7-c2b9-5972-b09e-a6f7847a9371" :answer-field/id #uuid 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)=\,-12{t}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{3})i+12{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{3})\,j,\,{T}^{′}(t)=-3{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{3})\,i-3{t}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{3})\,j\end{aligned}
$$"] ["question-941975f4-ea50-5edb-a299-e8568f71e188" :question/worked-solution "Since we are given both the derivative of the curve ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we find the magnitudes of ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-12{t}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{3}))}^{2}+{(12{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{3}))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-12{t}^{2})^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡({t}^{3})+(12{t}^{2})^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡({t}^{3})} \\  & =\sqrt{(12{t}^{2})^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡({t}^{3})+{cos}^{2}⁡({t}^{3}))} \\  & =12{t}^{2} \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-3{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{3}))}^{2}+{(-3{t}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{3}))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-3{t}^{2})^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡({t}^{3})+(-3{t}^{2})^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡({t}^{3})} \\  & =\sqrt{(3{t}^{2})^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡({t}^{3})+{cos}^{2}⁡({t}^{3}))} \\  & =3{t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{3{t}^{2}}{12{t}^{2}}=\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$"] ["question-941975f4-ea50-5edb-a299-e8568f71e188" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] ["answer-field-d2ae9bf6-e514-5558-98b8-e081859740e5" :answer-field/id #uuid a curve measures how much the curve "bends" at a given point. It can also be thought of as a measure of how much the curve deviates from being a straight line. Curvature is denoted by the Greek letter $\kappa$ (pronounced "kappa"). 

If $\kappa=0$ at some point on a curve, then that curve looks like a straight line in some neighborhood of the point.

If the curve $\mathbf{r}(s)$ is parametrized by the arc length $s,$ then the curvature $\kappa$ is the magnitude of the change of direction of the unit tangent vector $\mathbf T$ per unit of arc length. That is,

$$
\kappa(s) = \left\| \dfrac{\textrm{d}\mathbf T}{\textrm{d}s}  \right\|= \| \mathbf T'(s) \|.
$$

Note that $|| \mathbf v ||$ denotes the magnitude of the vector $\mathbf v.$

For example, suppose we are given the curve 

$$
\mathbf r(s)= \left\langle \sin\left(\dfrac s2\right), \: \dfrac{\sqrt{3}s}{2}, \: -\cos\left(\dfrac s2\right)\right\rangle
$$

 
which is parametrized by arc length $s.$ Let's find the curvature of  $\mathbf r(s)$  at the point where $s={\pi}.$

First, we find the unit tangent vector:

$$
\mathbf T(s) =\dfrac 12 \left\langle \cos\left( \dfrac s2\right), \: \sqrt{3}, \: \sin \left(\dfrac s2\right)\right\rangle
$$

 

Next, we differentiate $\mathbf{T}(s)$ and evaluate its absolute value at $s=\pi\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\sqrt{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2}))⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,0,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(\pi ) & =\frac{1}{4}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,0,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}⟨-1,\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain the curvature by taking the magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(\pi ) & =‖{T}^{′}(\pi )‖=\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{0}^{2}}=\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

 

**Note:** To calculate $\kappa,$ the function $\mathbf{r}(s)$ should be at least twice differentiable with respect to $s.$"] [17592186121007 :tutorial/content "If the curve $\mathbf r(t)$ is parametrized by a general parameter $t,$ then

$$

$$

$$

tangent vector of the curve is given by

$$
\mathbf T(s) = -\dfrac{4}{5}\sin{s}\,\mathbf i+\dfrac{3}{5} \sin{s}\, \mathbf j + \cos{s}\,\mathbf k.
$$" :question/worked-solution "Since we are given that $\mathbf{r}(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $\mathbf T(s)$ are both parametrized by the arc length $s,$ we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
\kappa(s) = \| \mathbf T'(s) \|
$$

Now, we differentiate $\mathbf T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and evaluate it at $s=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡s)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡s)j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡s)k \\  & =-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡s\,i+\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡s\,j-\operatorname{sin}⁡s\,k \\ {T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\,i+\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\,j-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\,k \\  & =0\,i+0\,j-k \\  & =-k\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain the curvature at the point where $s=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖=‖-k‖=\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}=1\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186048999} {:db/id 17592186051021} {:db/id 17592186120316 :question/id #uuid "3633992b-833e-5580-afa2-a5fd321c1b40" :question/math-academy-id "q-34268"} {:db/id 17592186120494 :question/id #uuid "ff2e0fe9-5f3d-51ba-a9a0-292022683d43" :question/math-academy-id "q-64584" :knowledge-point/_questions [{:db/id 17592186119748 :knowledge-point/id #uuid "9befd973-a2d9-567a-8808-d126ecaaae1b" :knowledge-point/title "Finding the Curvature Given the Arc Length Parametrization And the Unit Tangent"}] :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "b00855ab-cf4f-598c-98e3-70f570e975f1" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "1" :db/id 17592186119079} {:answer/id #uuid "de4ddacb-de2e-506b-9cd6-ca31cbd7387e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\frac{1}{3}" :db/id 17592186119080} {:answer/id #uuid "4ec4d528-3865-566e-b0f2-7928ad804460" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "3" :db/id 17592186119081} {:answer/id #uuid "71eb4d9d-bf87-5ee1-bab6-0262a42b7b26" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\sqrt{3}" :db/id 17592186119082} {:answer/id #uuid "73cab0bc-9afb-5a1a-827a-444f5929111e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "0" :db/id 17592186119083}] :answer-field/id #uuid "058516c5-41da-5120-8490-39e6081e2067" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493 :db/ident :answer-field.type/radio} :db/id 17592186119078}] :question/problem "Consider the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by arc length $s$. $\mathbf r(t) = \left\langle 2\sin t, \:2\cos t \right\rangle.$" :question/worked-solution "Let $\mathbf T(t)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the parameter $t.$ Since we are given the curve $\mathbf{r}(t)$ parametrized by the parameter $t$ (not the arc length $s$), we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
\mathbf \kappa(t) = \dfrac{\left\| \mathbf T'(t) \right\|}{\| \mathbf r'(t) \|}
$$

First, we calculate $\mathbf r'(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the corresponding unit tangent vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate $\mathbf T'(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186050685} {:db/id 17592186120299 :question/id #uuid "e8fb85a9-2192-5e5c-a901-e1b2f73eca00" :question/math-academy-id "q-34098"} {:db/id 17592186120305 :question/id #uuid $$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)=⟨2t,\,-3{t}^{2}⟩,\,{T}^{′}(t)=-\frac{6}{(9{t}^{2}+4)^{3/2}}⟨3t,\,2⟩,\,t\ge 0\end{aligned}
$$" :question/worked-solution "Since we are given both the derivative of the curve ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we find the magnitudes of ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{6}{(9{t}^{2}+4)^{3/2}}\cdot \sqrt{{(3t)}^{2}+{(2)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{6}{(9{t}^{2}+4)^{3/2}}\cdot \sqrt{9{t}^{2}+4} \\  & =\frac{6}{9{t}^{2}+4} \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(2t)}^{2}+{(-3{t}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+9{t}^{4}} \\  & =t\sqrt{9{t}^{2}+4}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{6}{9{t}^{2}+4})}{t\sqrt{9{t}^{2}+4}} \\  & =\frac{6}{t(9{t}^{2}+4)^{3/2}}.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186317268 :question/id #uuid "370f1619-74a5-5906-bb7b-088dc720563d" :question/math-academy-id "q-34245"} {:db/id 17592186335731 :question/id #uuid Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\  & =⟨t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ &  \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =t\end{aligned}
$$

since $t>0.$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}

Next, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, the curvature for  $t>0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{1}{t}.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186433629 :question/id #uuid "c48a3e25-1a31-5723-bb94-d587dcc4bb55" :question/math-academy-id "q-80546" :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "1251bed4-415d-5590-a871-e4a9657e13d3" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}" :db/id 17592186433617} {:answer/id #uuid "481e6b9f-c5af-58b8-b98e-c12965a43b0e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\sqrt{2}" :db/id 17592186433619} {:answer/id #uuid "c86e68ce-7275-5906-ac2f-57213bf72bac" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}" :db/id 17592186433622} {:answer/id #uuid "d87a76ef-7c66-5822-bbbd-0695f641dc2c" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "4" :db/id 17592186433623} {:answer/id #uuid "e5a5693f-64fa-5920-9519-f34d893234c3" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{4}" :db/id 17592186433625}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186433622} :answer-field/id #uuid "5ef00e22-7033-5539-a4d7-5c70d771c4f1" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186433627}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485} :question/problem "Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)$ given that its derivative ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the corresponding unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$ are as follows:

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)k \\  & =2t\,i+2t\,j+1\,k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(2t)^{2}+(2t)^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

   

Hence, the corresponding unit tangent vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}}(2t\,i+2t\,j+k).\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{(\frac{\sqrt{8}\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}}{{(8{t}^{2}+1)}^{3/2}})}{\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}}=\frac{\sqrt{8}}{{(8{t}^{2}+1)}^{3/2}}.\end{aligned}

$$

$$
r(s)=⟨s-2\operatorname{arctan}⁡s,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡({s}^{2}+1)⟩,\,s\ge 0.
$$" :question/worked-solution "Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(s-2\operatorname{arctan}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({s}^{2}+1))⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{{s}^{2}-1}{{s}^{2}+1},\,\frac{2s}{{s}^{2}+1}⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{{s}^{2}-1}{{s}^{2}+1}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{2s}{{s}^{2}+1})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{4s}{({s}^{2}+1)^{2}},\,\frac{2(1-{s}^{2})}{({s}^{2}+1)^{2}}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{({s}^{2}+1)^{2}}⟨4s,\,2(1-{s}^{2})⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =\frac{1}{({s}^{2}+1)^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{(4s)^{2}+{(2(1-{s}^{2}))}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{({s}^{2}+1)^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{16{s}^{2}+4{s}^{4}-8{s}^{2}+4} \\  & =\frac{1}{({s}^{2}+1)^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{4{s}^{4}+8{s}^{2}+4} \\  & =\frac{1}{({s}^{2}+1)^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{4({s}^{2}+1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2({s}^{2}+1)}{({s}^{2}+1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{{s}^{2}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186317250 :question/id #uuid "41d7c399-26f9-5663-8418-176ada36a15d" :question/math-academy-id "q-34238"} {:db/id 17592186348404 :question/id #uuid [{:db/id 17592186120580 :step/content {:db/id 17592186121002 :tutorial/content "The **curvature** of a curve measures how much the curve "bends" at a given point. It can also be thought of as a measure of how much the curve deviates from being a straight line. Curvature is denoted by the Greek letter $\kappa$ (pronounced "kappa"). 

If $\kappa=0$ at some point on a curve, then that curve looks like a straight line in some neighborhood of the point.

If the curve $\mathbf{r}(s)$ is parametrized by the arc length $s,$ then the curvature $\kappa$ is the magnitude of the change of direction of the unit tangent vector $\mathbf T$ per unit of arc length. That is,

$$
\kappa(s) = \left\| \dfrac{\textrm{d}\mathbf T}{\textrm{d}s}  \right\|= \| \mathbf T'(s) \|.
$$

Note that $|| \mathbf v ||$ denotes the magnitude of the vector $\mathbf v.$

For example, suppose we are given the curve 

$$
\mathbf r(s)= \left\langle \sin\left(\dfrac s2\right), \: \dfrac{\sqrt{3}s}{2}, \: -\cos\left(\dfrac s2\right)\right\rangle
$$

 
which is parametrized by arc length $s.$ Let's find the curvature of  $\mathbf r(s)$  at the point where $s={\pi}.$

First, we find the unit tangent vector:

$$
\mathbf T(s) =\dfrac 12 \left\langle \cos\left( \dfrac s2\right), \: \sqrt{3}, \: \sin \left(\dfrac s2\right)\right\rangle
$$

 

Next, we differentiate $\mathbf{T}(s)$ and evaluate its absolute value at $s=\pi\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{'}(s) & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}(\frac{s}{2})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\sqrt{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}(\frac{s}{2}))⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}⟨-\operatorname{sin}(\frac{s}{2}),\,0,\,\operatorname{cos}(\frac{s}{2})⟩ \\ {T}^{'}(\pi ) & =\frac{1}{4}⟨-\operatorname{sin}(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,0,\,\operatorname{cos}(\frac{\pi }{2})⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}⟨-1,\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain the curvature by taking the magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(\pi ) & =‖{T}^{'}(\pi )‖=\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{0}^{2}}=\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

 

**Note:** To calculate $\kappa,$ the function $\mathbf{r}(s)$ should be at least twice differentiable with respect to $s.$" :tutorial/id #uuid "d74577d5-5fe6-5544-bd86-b20fee42defa" :question/math-academy-id "q-64696" :question/problem "Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)={t}^{2}\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+t\,k.$" :question/worked-solution "Let $T(t)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the parameter $t.$ Since we are given the curve $r(t)$ parametrized by the parameter $t$ (not the arc length $s$), we will use the following formula for the curvature: 

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)k \\  & =2t\,i+2t\,j+1\,k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(2t)^{2}+(2t)^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

   

Hence, the corresponding unit tangent vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}}(2t\,i+2t\,j+k).\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2t}{\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2t}{\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}})\,k \\  & =\frac{1}{{(8{t}^{2}+1)}^{3/2}}(2\,i+2\,j-8t\,k) \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-8t)^{2}}}{{(8{t}^{2}+1)}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{8+{8}^{2}{t}^{2}}}{{(8{t}^{2}+1)}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{8(1+8{t}^{2})}}{{(8{t}^{2}+1)}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{8}\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}}{{(8{t}^{2}+1)}^{3/2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{(\frac{\sqrt{8}\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}}{{(8{t}^{2}+1)}^{3/2}})}{\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}}=\frac{\sqrt{8}}{{(8{t}^{2}+1)}^{3/2}}.\end{aligned}
$$"} :step/id #uuid "00d70dc7-07a1-5030-82b3-0ddd637fbfb1" :step/next {:db/id 17592186433632}} {:db/id 17592186433632 :step/content {:db/id 17592186120495 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "d0c9c1f0-df55-556e-833a-7fb64732dde4" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\sqrt{2}" :db/id 17592186119085} {:answer/id #uuid "f30dc2a4-65fc-5750-b501-c7c5b426ccda" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "8" :db/id 17592186119086} {:answer/id #uuid "092a0aaf-082d-545c-9806-110ce43d35b1" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "1" :db/id 17592186119087} {:answer/id #uuid "3ef17328-d207-5798-8681-f24753e09c81" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "4" :db/id 17592186119088} {:answer/id #uuid "62750844-6757-5328-89ca-54678ebfa45e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2" :db/id 17592186119089}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186119087} :answer-field/id #uuid "4ccd57a8-0a01-50d0-ac4b-6f5f8f6b6e44" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186119084}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "4163ce17-8c2e-5e7a-b5d2-d7191ad32de0" :question/math-academy-id "q-64700" :question/problem "Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where

$$

$$" :question/worked-solution "Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡s,\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s,\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡s,\,-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s,\,-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is  

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{(-\operatorname{cos}⁡s)}^{2}+{(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s)}^{2}+{(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡s+\frac{1}{2}{sin}^{2}⁡s+\frac{1}{2}{sin}^{2}⁡s} \\  & =\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡s+{sin}^{2}⁡s} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)=⟨-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,-4\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)⟩,\,{T}^{′}(t)=⟨-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩\end{aligned}
$$" :question/worked-solution "Since we are given both the derivative of the curve ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$

$$

Now, we find the magnitudes of ${T}^{′}(t)$ and ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))}^{2}+{(2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)+4{sin}^{2}⁡(2t)} \\  & =\sqrt{4({cos}^{2}⁡(2t)+{sin}^{2}⁡(2t))} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2 \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))^{2}+(-4\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16{sin}^{2}⁡(2t)+16{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)} \\  & =\sqrt{16({sin}^{2}⁡(2t)+{cos}^{2}⁡(2t))} \\  & =\sqrt{16} \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{\,2\,}{4}=\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$"} :step/id #uuid "cb9b8003-d330-530b-a31a-213d60c41132"}] :activity/title "Introduction to Curvature" :activity/type {:db/id 17592186045464 :db/ident :activity.type/review} :db/id 17592186433616} {:db/id 17592186046660} {:db/id 17592186433631 :step/content {:db/id 17592186433630 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "1367431b-f708-53d0-907c-401baf44b1b0" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\sqrt{2}" :db/id 17592186433618} {:answer/id #uuid "5ddff454-cafc-5d0a-8e73-761ad50a723b" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{2}}{{(8{t}^{2}+2)}^{3/2}}" :db/id 17592186433620} {:answer/id #uuid "ae9b1f32-4af7-5ccc-b6f9-f8acc59e69d0" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{8}}{{(8{t}^{2}+1)}^{3/2}}" :db/id 17592186433621} {:answer/id #uuid "e1ed4446-c062-507c-a44a-cf42f43f3e0d" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2\sqrt{3}" :db/id 17592186433624} {:answer/id #uuid "f9cd5e7a-fd43-5ce4-9986-155332afc1c4" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "4" :db/id 17592186433626}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186433621} :answer-field/id #uuid "c90f0f81-e6f6-5365-9a31-9800a129aea5" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186433628}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045486} :question/id #uuid "d3e668b2-3360-5bad-970e-ebd786d68368" :question/math-academy-id "q-64696" :question/problem "Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)={t}^{2}\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+t\,k.$" :question/worked-solution "Let $T(t)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the parameter $t.$ Since we are given the curve $r(t)$ parametrized by the parameter $t$ (not the arc length $s$), we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$

$$

$$

Now, we find the magnitudes of ${T}^{′}(t)$ and ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{\,2\,}{4}=\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}

the core mathematical structures and analytical tools used throughout theoretical and applied physics. Building on calculus and introductory linear algebra, the course introduces vector geometry, multivariable analysis, and differential equations in a unified framework designed for modeling physical systems.
Students learn how mathematical concepts such as vector spaces, linear transformations, multivariable functions, and differential equations provide the language and computational techniques used to describe motion, fields, and dynamical processes. The course emphasizes connections between abstract mathematical ideas and the physical principles they support, preparing students for advanced study in classical mechanics, electromagnetism, and related areas of physics." 17592186045417] [17592186046659 1009 "The course begins with foundational topics that support later mathematical modeling in physics. Students study vector geometry in three-dimensional space, including equations of lines and planes and geometric relationships between them. These tools appear naturally in the description of trajectories, rays, and intersections of physical surfaces. Introductory set theory provides a precise language for describing mathematical structures and regions in space, supporting later work in multivariable analysis and probability.
Students then develop computational tools from linear algebra. Methods such as Gaussian elimination, matrix inverses, determinants, and LU factorization are used to analyze and solve systems of linear equations. These techniques arise when solving coupled equations in physical models, such as electrical circuits, mechanical systems with multiple interacting components, and discretized approximations of physical fields.
The course next develops the structure of vector spaces and linear transformations. Students study spans, bases, dimension, rank, and null spaces, and extend these ideas to abstract vector spaces. Linear maps and their matrix representations are examined, establishing the connection between geometric transformations and matrix algebra. These ideas culminate in the study of eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and matrix diagonalization, which are central tools for solving differential equations describing oscillations, normal modes of vibration, and stability of dynamical systems.
The course then turns to multivariable calculus and vector analysis. Students analyze functions of several variables, quadric surfaces, and coordinate transformations. Partial derivatives, gradients, and the multivariable chain rule are developed along with linear approximations and higher-order derivatives. These concepts describe how physical quantities such as temperature, pressure, or electric potential vary in space. Vector-valued functions and vector fields are studied together with curvature, divergence, and curl, providing the mathematical language used to describe velocity fields in fluid flow and electric and magnetic fields in electromagnetism.
Students then study multiple integration, focusing on double integrals and coordinate transformations such as polar coordinates. These techniques allow the computation of physical quantities distributed over regions, such as mass, charge, or probability density.
The final portion of the course introduces differential equations as models of dynamical systems. Students study first-order equations and qualitative behavior of solutions through phase-line analysis. Applications include motion under drag, gravitational attraction, electrical circuits, and population dynamics. The course concludes with second-order linear differential equations and oscillatory systems, including harmonic motion, damped oscillators, and resonance—fundamental mathematical models for vibrating continues the development of advanced mathematical techniques used throughout modern physics. Building on the analytical framework established in the first course, students study orthogonality, multivariable integration, vector calculus theorems, and advanced methods for differential equations.
The course emphasizes mathematical structures that arise naturally in physics, including inner product spaces, orthogonal projections, integral theorems of vector calculus, and transform methods for solving differential equations. These tools provide the mathematical foundation for analyzing electromagnetic fields, wave phenomena, dynamical systems, and statistical models encountered in advanced physics courses." 17592186045417] [17592186046660 1009 "The course begins with the theory of projections in inner product spaces. Students study norms, inner products, orthogonality, and orthogonal complements in vector spaces over the real and complex numbers. Techniques such as orthogonal projections, the Gram–Schmidt process, and QR factorization allow vectors to be decomposed into orthogonal components. These ideas play a role in Fourier analysis, signal decomposition, and numerical methods used in physical simulations.
Students then explore quadratic forms and the diagonalization of symmetric matrices. The spectral theorem provides a geometric interpretation of symmetric transformations and leads to techniques for analyzing energy functions and stability in physical systems. Singular value decomposition is also introduced as a powerful matrix factorization with applications in numerical modeling and data analysis.
Applications of linear algebra follow, including least-squares methods for solving overdetermined systems. These methods arise when fitting theoretical models to experimental data and when approximating solutions to physical equations.
The course then develops multivariable integration in three dimensions. Students compute triple integrals over general regions and apply coordinate transformations such as cylindrical and spherical coordinates. These techniques allow physicists to compute quantities such as mass distributions, charge densities, and gravitational or electric potentials.
Students next study line integrals and surface integrals of scalar and vector fields. Concepts such as circulation, flux, and path independence lead to the fundamental theorems of vector calculus, including Green’s theorem, the divergence theorem, and Stokes’ theorem. These results form the mathematical framework underlying conservation laws and the differential and integral formulations of electromagnetic theory.
Applications of multivariable calculus follow, including vector mechanics and optimization. Students analyze motion using vector-valued functions, apply Newton’s second law to systems in the plane, and study work–energy relationships. Multiple integrals are used to compute mass, centers of mass, moments of inertia, and other physical quantities.
The course then returns to differential equations, extending earlier techniques to systems of linear differential equations. Students analyze dynamical systems using eigenvalues, phase portraits, and matrix methods, which appear in models of interacting systems such as coupled oscillators or predator–prey dynamics.
Laplace transforms are introduced as a powerful tool for solving linear differential equations with discontinuous inputs or initial conditions. Boundary value problems and Fourier series are then developed, providing mathematical techniques used to solve differential equations describing heat flow, vibrating strings, wave propagation, and other physical phenomena.
The course concludes with numerical methods for differential equations and advanced probability topics. Students analyze the accuracy and stability of numerical schemes used in computational physics and study multivariate probability distributions and the central limit theorem, which appear in If $\kappa=0$ at some point on a curve, then that curve looks like a straight line in some neighborhood of the point.

If the curve $\mathbf{r}(s)$ is parametrized by the arc length $s,$ then the curvature $\kappa$ is the magnitude of the change of direction of the unit tangent vector $\mathbf T$ per unit of arc length. That is,

$$
\kappa(s) = \left\| \dfrac{\textrm{d}\mathbf T}{\textrm{d}s}  \right\|= \| \mathbf T'(s) \|.
$$

Note that $|| \mathbf v ||$ denotes the magnitude of the vector $\mathbf v.$

For example, suppose we are given the curve 

$$
\mathbf r(s)= \left\langle \sin\left(\dfrac s2\right), \: \dfrac{\sqrt{3}s}{2}, \: -\cos\left(\dfrac s2\right)\right\rangle
$$

First, we find the unit tangent vector:

$$
\mathbf T(s) =\dfrac 12 \left\langle \cos\left( \dfrac s2\right), \: \sqrt{3}, \: \sin \left(\dfrac s2\right)\right\rangle
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{'}(s) & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}(\frac{s}{2})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\sqrt{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}(\frac{s}{2}))⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}⟨-\operatorname{sin}(\frac{s}{2}),\,0,\,\operatorname{cos}(\frac{s}{2})⟩ \\ {T}^{'}(\pi ) & =\frac{1}{4}⟨-\operatorname{sin}(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,0,\,\operatorname{cos}(\frac{\pi }{2})⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}⟨-1,\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain the curvature by taking the magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(\pi ) & =‖{T}^{'}(\pi )‖=\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{0}^{2}}=\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
